feature: Cutting while a video plays keeps it playing (pass 28)
summary: Split at Playhead (Command B) pressed while a video plays now cuts the clip and play carries on, the way Final Cut's Blade and Premiere's Add Edit do. Before, every cut stopped play, and stopping cost the window a 20 ms wait on the system that draws it.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no switch changed from its default (the new switch 'Cutting keeps playing' is on by default in Next). Measured on the probe with a profiled edits-only walk and the speed walk on the 6 minute reference edit. The reference edit's folder for File > Open: ~/Library/Caches/Photonz Reference Edit/Photonz Dev

try.do: Open the 6 minute reference edit in Photonz Dev with the button below.
Click a clip on V1 to pick it, then press Space to play.
Press Command B while it plays: the clip is cut and play carries on.
Press Command B again a moment later, then Space to stop.
Press Command Z twice: the clip is whole again.

evaluate: Is it right that a cut made while playing leaves play running, as in Final Cut and Premiere?
After a cut while playing, is the piece before the cut the one you expect to have picked?
Does cutting while it plays feel smooth, with no hitch in the picture?
rough: Edits with a clip picked still miss the 16 ms bar: blade 21 to 24 ms (its longest pass is now the cut's panel section landing, not the stop), a pick 25 to 33, unpick 29 to 37, a pick from nothing 24 to 45. That is this task's own bar (a-long-edit-with-transitions-plays-scrubs-and-ed).

What is left of a pick is SwiftUI and AppKit work with no app code over 2 ms under it: layout of the new rows, the accessibility focus walk and the title bar's drag regions, about 15 ms a pass whatever lands (a-long-edit-with-transitions-plays-scrubs-and-ed).
Worst scrub lag 1 is still not reached; this pass did not work on scrubbing (a-long-edit-with-transitions-plays-scrubs-and-ed).
